changes.before: Implement shutdownState(active,elapsed,deadline). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Before a server stops, let current work finish within a set time limit.

before: Graceful shutdown stops accepting new work and gives active work a bounded chance to finish. An unbounded wait can leave a process stuck forever.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.

The first branch stops when no active work remains. Otherwise the deadline comparison distinguishes waiting from timeout. A deadline result does not prove unfinished work succeeded; the surrounding service must define cancellation and recovery.

Read the function call shutdownState(0, 0, 100) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, shutdownState runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
The deadline arrives while two jobs remain active. What can this helper honestly report? The deadline bounds waiting. It provides no success receipt for unfinished work.
after: Graceful shutdown means stopping new requests while giving current work a chance to finish. This waiting stage is called draining.
Set a deadline so the server cannot wait forever. Here elapsed is the time already spent waiting. deadline is the allowed wait, in the same units.
Return "stop" when active is 0. Otherwise return "deadline" when elapsed >= deadline, or "drain" while there is still time.
Reaching the deadline does not mean every job succeeded. The service must decide how to stop or recover unfinished work.
Try two active jobs exactly at the time limit. The result is "deadline". Try zero active jobs at the same time: the result is "stop" because no work remains.

project.title: Drain active work before stopping
project.task: Complete shutdownState(active,elapsed,deadline). Return "stop" when active is 0. Otherwise return "deadline" if elapsed >= deadline, or "drain" if time remains.
